reuse.why: Most actions share getFillableCategories and existing budget infrastructure, but copyPreviousMonth repeats eligibility rules and FIXED_TAG reimplements the shared tag parser.

duplication.why: The diff consolidates category queries but duplicates eligibility filtering, tag recognition, and the new consumer's income eligibility guard.

placement.why: Budget selection and handler registration follow existing layers, although tag recognition belongs in the existing shared tags module.

scope.why: The edits remain focused on the requested month-wide actions, their registration, tests, and release notes.

maintainability.why: The shared selector improves ownership, but maintaining parallel eligibility implementations and a separate tag grammar invites future divergence.

bypasses_abstraction.where: actions.ts: copyPreviousMonth bypasses getFillableCategories, and FIXED_TAG bypasses extractTagsFromText in shared/tags.ts.

disguised_duplication.where: actions.ts: copyPreviousMonth expresses hidden/template/fixed eligibility as an imperative guard while getFillableCategories expresses the same rules through SQL and array filtering.

abstraction_drift.where: getFillableCategories gains includeHiddenCategories and conditional SQL filtering, while copyPreviousMonth independently implements the evolving eligibility policy.
